messages.subject: off grid on real line
parts:
Hi Group,

I am wondering if the LGCP model is implemented with the SPDE approximation on the real line? The examples in the off grid paper are all spatial point processes and uses the triangulation/mesh, so I wonder? Can I just add one dimension and assume my observations are on a square instead by adding constant height?

Thank you, any comment will be much appreciated!

~Julia

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: off grid on real line
parts:
Hi!

Since the LGCP/SPDE construction is done through "clever" use of the observation matrix feature (control.predictor(A=...)) one can in principle apply it to any of the one-dimensional models on the real line, such as "rw2".

I am also adding wrapper functions to construct SPDE models on the real line, with "1D-mesh" objects to help with the book-keeping.  This experimental feature can be found in functions currently containing the name "inla.mesh.1d".  I think the only really missing link to using nearly identical code to the one for the triangulated meshes in the paper is the wrapper function for constructing the SPDE model object for a one-dimensional mesh, or to add support for this in the inla.spde2.matern wrapper.  I hope to have this fully implemented and documented in late February or March.

Later, we hope to have more user-friendly LGCP-wrappers around the basic SPDE-wrappers; some of this already exists but is not fully documented yet.

/Finn

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: off grid on real line
parts: >I received also comment about using GMRF but I am actually interested in the continuous part: GRF. I don't understand why one could use rw2 in principle.

The RW2 model in 1D implements the continuous model found in Lindgren and Rue 2008 (from SJS). This was a prototype of the models more fully described in Lindgren, Rue and Lindström (2011) that used piecewise linear basis functions and the finite element method to construct a GMRF approximation to the continuous GRF.  So if you construct an "A matrix" yourself (or possibly use the experimental code - I don't know the details of that, sorry), you can use an intrinsic model in 1D with alpha=2.
> I thought the point of the SPDE solution is that it worked for the Matern class and the simplest on 1 D I could think off is the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process.

The important distinction here is the SPDE *model*, which work with the Matern class, and the SPDE *code* in INLA, which is currently only implemented fully in 2D.  As Finn said above, we are getting to it, but it isn't done yet.  Unfortunately, with a project of this size, we have to build the code "as needed" (or at least "in order of priority").

Best wishes,

Dan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: off grid on real line
parts:
Short reply: the rw2 (on R) is a special case of the Matern models (SPDE with alpha=2, kappa=0).  Ornstein-Uhlenbeck is another special case (alpha=1, kappa>0). rw1 corresponds to alpha=1, kappa=0.  The key to the LGCP models, regardless of which GRF model is used lies in the continuous space/time interpretation.  That the calculations are carried out using GMRFs can be viewed as just a computational implementation detail. (An important detail, but detail nonetheless...)
/Finn
